name: Harryedic
body: I am trying to make a small secondhand work wardrobe feel coherent without replacing everything. My work clothes are mostly secondhand, so finding the right size already limits which colors are available. I would like a few pieces that work together instead of a collection of individually appealing bargains. A charcoal jacket and two cream shirts are staying, because they fit well and get worn regularly. A lightweight knit would fill the main gap, but the local selection will only offer a few colors. Should the first comparison involve my existing jacket and shirts, or should I assess each color beside my face? One subject behind this question is [url=https://bodytypes.top]personal color analysis[/url] and I would prefer a practical method that does not require throwing out useful clothes or chasing perfect matches. Which observations would you record after trying a piece so that future choices become easier to compare?
